assumptions: Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop (OVRServiceLauncher.exe) are deployed on the same host.
The browser HTML injection vulnerability reliably achieves local process execution despite the description stating it can only 'potentially execute code'.

evidence_quotes.quote: inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code
expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation

missing_conditions: Proof of co-location/same-host deployment of Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop.
Confirmation that the UI injection actually yields local process execution rather than UI spoofing alone.
Environment compatibility confirming that the browser execution context can interact with OVRServiceLauncher.exe handles.
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 allows an attacker to inject HTML into the Oculus Browser UI to spoof UI and 'potentially execute code'. CVE-2021-24038 requires 'an unprivileged process' on a host running OVRServiceLauncher.exe to exploit handle management for local privilege escalation. While local code execution could satisfy the prerequisite of an unprivileged process, the source effect is modal ('potentially execute code') and same-host deployment across these distinct Oculus components cannot be inferred from absence of data, rendering the transition conditional.
